bull.b: The long-term Anthropic lease provides substantial contracted demand for TeraWulf’s AI infrastructure platform. Google credit support strengthens the financing framework, improving revenue visibility and creating a durable foundation for future data-center cash generation.

Rapid growth in HPC leasing revenue shows that TeraWulf is converting data-center capacity into a larger operating business. Continued Lake Mariner commissioning and planned capacity additions could support meaningful revenue expansion beyond bitcoin mining.

Substantial reported liquidity, expanded credit capacity, and Fluor’s comprehensive EPC role give TeraWulf resources and execution structure for contracted projects. These supports improve its ability to fund construction and manage complex delivery milestones.

bear.b: Extremely negative operating and net margins show that revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable company-wide profitability. Persistent losses can limit internal reinvestment, increase reliance on financing, and make future earnings highly sensitive to execution.

Deeply negative operating and free cash flow indicate that TeraWulf is consuming substantial cash while expanding its platform. Continued burn increases funding requirements and leaves less internally generated capital available for construction, debt service, or resilience.

The remaining Wolfe Compute capital requirement creates meaningful execution and financing exposure even with contracted demand. Large committed expenditures can pressure liquidity and returns if construction timing, financing costs, or project economics worsen.
